sections.currentVisual: [Verified by reading] Two things move. (1) THE BENCH (Bench.tsx, mounted at Skills.tsx:106 above the table): a bipartite 'cabling' diagram. Rails are real HTML <button>s - 13 sources in three bands (Programmes/Repositories/Credentials, Bench.tsx:73-77) on the left, 17 capabilities on the right - and only the 20 wires are SVG: cubic Beziers with flat tangents (Bench.tsx:138-139) whose endpoints are measured from layout (getBoundingClientRect on every node, Bench.tsx:114-150), re-measured by a ResizeObserver with a two-rAF settle and again on document.fonts.ready (Bench.tsx:152-184). Stroke is one of two userSpaceOnUse linearGradients spanning the board width: gold (stops 0.06/0.62/0.62/0.06 alpha, Bench.tsx:289-301) for the 17 production wires, --mist-400 grey (0.05/0.5/0.5/0.05, Bench.tsx:302-314) for the 3 non-production wires; the pending capability has no wire. Trace-in: once, when an IntersectionObserver at threshold 0.15 fires (Bench.tsx:196-207), CSS keyframe `trace` (stroke-dasharray 1 1, dashoffset 1->0 with pathLength=1, Bench.module.css:72-83) at --motion-cine 900ms / --motion-ease-emphasized with per-wire delay 120+index*38ms (Bench.tsx:333, Bench.module.css:56); a 1780ms timer (120+20*38+820+80, Bench.tsx:209-214) then flags data-settled and the animation is removed so resizes never replay it. Attention: hover/focus on any node sets data-dimmed on the board; unconnected wires drop to stroke-opacity 0.12, connected ones go to 1 and width 1.4 (Bench.module.css:100-107); unconnected nodes to opacity 0.3 (Bench.module.css:186-194); a fixed-height readout (min-height 5.2rem, Bench.module.css:241-251) prints the capability's evidence or the source's link count; selecting a capability also marks the table row data-traced with a 2px inset gold rule (Skills.tsx:41,184; Skills.module.css:392-395). Status marks: gold filled dot for production, half-filled grey for non-production, open ring for pending (Bench.module.css:210-238). (2) THE CARD: `cardSettle` opacity 0->1 at --motion-fast 200ms on mount (Skills.module.css:59-74); filter chips transition colour/border/background 200ms. Filtering hides rows with the `hidden` attribute inside a wrapper whose min-height is the measured unfiltered table (Skills.tsx:43-78,148-151). Tech: SVG + CSS + React state; NO WebGL, NO framer-motion in this section. Reduced-motion path: Bench.tsx:195-198 short-circuits to drawn=true, Bench.module.css:85-90 sets `.wire[data-drawn]{animation:none;opacity:1}`, Skills.module.css:379-387 removes the card fade and chip transitions; the global whitelist at app/globals.css:941-957 drops the stroke-opacity/stroke-width transitions so dimming is instant. No-WebGL path: identical to default (nothing here uses GL). Narrow path (<=900px, Bench.module.css:285-349): the wires SVG is display:none, the source rail becomes a row of tappable chips and the capability rail a plain list - the diagram is absent on phones and portrait tablets. Cost: 20 <path>s, 30 buttons, one ResizeObserver, one IntersectionObserver, ~30 getBoundingClientRect reads per measure, two rAFs per resize; no per-frame work at rest.
sections.story: [Verified by reading skills.ts:1-20 and Skills.tsx:19-35] The section argues 'calibration card, not skill cloud': every capability has evidence, the status names the ENVIRONMENT the evidence came from (production / outside production / not yet held), never a proficiency, and the last row - 'AWS and GCP certification: studying; no certificate issued' (skills.ts:213-220) - is the credibility anchor that makes the rows above it believable. The Bench draws that argument: each capability wired to the programme, repository or issuing body it came from, gold only where it ran in production. On a desktop the drawing carries the story well - the graph IS the proof that the list is not adjectives. It fails to carry it in three places: (a) below 900px the wires vanish and the reader gets a chip filter plus a list, i.e. exactly the 'list of adjectives' the component's own docblock says it exists to avoid (Bench.tsx:15-20 vs Bench.module.css:285-288); (b) the same fact is echoed on three surfaces at once (readout, gold-ruled table row, node label), so the 'one visual' is diluted; (c) the trace-in is a one-shot time-based reveal rather than something the reader's own scroll or attention drives, so on a fast scroll it has finished before it is watched.

sections.story: [Verified by reading vitrine.ts:1-14 and Vitrine.tsx:16-30] 'Six of thirty-eight': the section argues that selection is an editorial act - six plates, each printing what its repository does NOT do (limits), three named exclusions with reasons, and metrics harvested from the GitHub API on a printed date rather than typed or live. The visual metaphor is a gallery vitrine: the reader's own scroll moves the spotlight, neighbours fall into shadow. The drawings are the strongest idea - 'never a screenshot, a logo or a laptop mockup; a mechanism drawing shows what it does' (Drawings.tsx:8-17) - but today they are still frames: the guard never strikes the claim, the push never rebuilds, the loop never runs, the caliper never closes. So the 'cinematic' content of the section is an opacity change, and the six drawings that actually tell each repository's story tell it silently. Gold is used correctly here and only on live URLs (Vitrine.module.css:257-265) - the one section where the gold rule is fully honoured.

sections.story: [Verified by reading listen.ts:1-14 and Listen.tsx:8-18] 'Always willing to listen - Feedback & coffee?': the closing screen is designed as the silence after five screens of instrumentation - one sentence of disposition (the only line on the site that carries no source, because it makes no factual claim), one hairline, four real anchors (mailto, tel, LinkedIn, GitHub), and a coffee line. No form by design: on a static export a form either lies about where the message goes or hands the visitor to a third party (Listen.tsx:14-17). The visual is meant to be 'the caliper at one-pixel scale: the last stroke the instrument makes' (Listen.tsx:33). It half-carries that: the stroke is never seen (it plays at load, not on arrival), and it is painted gold - the one colour the site reserves for a sourced figure - under a sentence the copy itself says is unsourced. The section's own CSS comments argue against the choice twice (Listen.module.css:113-115 'gold is reserved for evidence'; 152-154 'an offer of coffee is not evidence'). For the Owner's brief this section is the hardest: its stated intent is to own almost nothing, so its one cinematic beat must be the quietest on the page.
